extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL body models. The dataset contains over 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects and more than 11000 motions.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1 [cs.CV]
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS unifies 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets by converting mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes using MoSh++. The method works for arbitrary marker sets, while recovering soft-tissue dynamics and realistic hand motion.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. A weight-balancing factor q is introduced that adjusts the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset combines 15 existing motion capture datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. Each dataset was recorded using a different number of markers (ranging from 37 to 91 markers) placed at different locations on the body.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ converts mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters through a two-stage optimization process. Stage I optimizes poses for 12 randomly chosen frames, a single shape, and latent marker positions. Stage II optimizes pose for each frame of mocap in the sequence while keeping latent marker locations and body shape parameters constant, and also optimizes for soft-tissue deformation coefficients.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out. The method uses Threshold Acceptance method as a fast annealing strategy to help avoid local optima, with 4 annealing stages of graduated optimization.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ method using SMPL/DMPL body models and MANO hand model. Powell's gradient based dogleg minimization implemented in the Chumpy autodifferentiation package.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared and will continue to expand the dataset.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape information is captured as part of the dataset. The dataset includes 346 subjects with varying body shapes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The method's runtime is not real-time. Current average runtimes are approximately 25 minutes per motion sequence for Stage I, 0.5 seconds per frame for Stage II without dynamics, and 2 seconds per frame for Stage II with dynamics. The method requires manual inspection and correction of results due to inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning. The dataset can enable machine learning applications in animation and computer vision. Users can ignore body shape and soft tissue deformations if they only care about pose, or normalize all bodies to the same shape using the SMPL shape space.
